title: Polite Japanese and the volitional
summary: ます is a helper verb on the い-stem, です is the polite だ, and the volitional (お-stem + う) says "let's" or "I intend to".

blocks.text: Until now the course has used the **plain** forms. The polite forms (the course says "formal"; the proper word is **polite**, 丁寧語) change only how you sound, not what you say.

**ます** is a helper verb that attaches to the **い-stem**. It changes politeness only. Its past is regular (**ました**), but its negative is **ません**, and the polite negative past is **ませんでした**. That one is simply worth memorizing.

blocks.en: Every morning (I) walk in the park.

blocks.jp: 昨日は歩きませんでした。

blocks.text: **です** is the polite form of **だ**. After a **noun or な-adjective** it is a real copula. After an **い-adjective** (赤いです) it adds only politeness, since 赤い already carries "is". Polite speech can also put です after ない: **話さないです**.
The **volitional** attaches to the **お-stem** and adds **う** (ichidan: **よう**). It expresses will: "let's" or "I will". It is not desire; for desire use たい. The polite volitional is **ましょう**.
だろう and でしょう
The volitional of the copula, **だろう / でしょう**, means "probably" or "I think".

items: **い-stem + ます**; negative **ません**; past **ました**; negative past **ませんでした**.
**です** after nouns and な-words is a copula; after い-adjectives it is only polite.
**Volitional = お-stem + う** (ichidan: **よう**); polite **ましょう**.
